analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation-only, in docs/architecture/security/attestation.md. No patch hunks, source code or tests were provided. I reviewed base lines 264-526 and head lines 1-262. Head lines 263 onward and the actual diff were not shown, so the whole-file comparison is incomplete.

New or changed head text is the 'Provider connection control' section (head lines 42-70) and the 2026-10-12 date. It says ProviderLoop+Serve.swift handles app_attest_shadow, trust_status and connection invalidation independently of the ordered model/inference consumer. Connect, disconnect and stream termination clear the old local grant and invalidate the previous App Attest task generation. The native Apple call is uncancellable, but a late callback cannot send an old session's proof over a replacement connection once the reader has processed invalidation. The text also says there is no new retry, grace period or trusted lifetime, and that the coordinator still verifies fresh evidence and enforces expiry and revocation.

This matches the canonical review note of 2026-10-10. It is consistent with TB-011, TB-002 and T-053 (stale authorization after a connection change), T-057 (availability) and T-052.

The docs state the binding and expiry invariants (head lines 10, 19, 79). The next pass should check that the Swift code actually does this: generation-checked proof send after the uncancellable callback, and clearing a replacement connection's grant on delayed cleanup. It should also check that coordinator-side final-handoff and expiry enforcement in coordinator/registry/inference_authorization.go and coordinator/registry/app_attest_authorization.go are unchanged.

Minor documentation inconsistency, not a security finding: the head runtime-manifest table (line 252) calls the routing gates 5 and 6, while the base gate table numbers them 6 and 7.
